items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: He told everybody that Eleanor Roosevelt and I were his two favorite writers.

ctx.x: That’s interesting because he was so smooth and debonair in person but it didn’t translate.

But he held information back and he didn’t tell the truth you know. When I was 18, I was a size 18. I was fat, I was awkward, I had no poise — well I still don’t have too much poise, but I was really uugh, it was terrible. And he said to me, because he knew he had me going, I believed everything he said. He said, “you know I’d like you to do something for me.” Oh by now I had a job on a newspaper, that was it. So he told everybody that Eleanor Roosevelt and I were his two favorite writers. I thought gee, that’s…
I hope you’re not tired of talking about your film.
